hero.title: Forward Deployed Engineer Roadmap
hero.subtitle: Work at the intersection of customer, product, engineering and AI. 10 stages — click any stage to jump.

capabilities: Build full-stack and AI prototypes customers can evaluate
Run discovery and translate business goals into scoped use cases
Design UI/UX and architecture under real enterprise constraints
Ship POCs and MVPs with clear evaluation and production gaps
Deploy with observability and pass security and executive reviews
Deliver an end-to-end capstone engagement pack

faq.question: How long does this roadmap take?
faq.answer: 12 weeks at 1 hour a day, 5 days a week — about 60 hours total. Move on when you meet each stage's "ready to move on" checkpoint, not only when the week band ends.

faq.question: What does the roadmap cover?
faq.answer: Ten stages: Software Engineering, AI Engineering, FDE SDLC (business requirements, UI/UX, architecture), Proof of concept, MVP, Production deployment, Enterprise AI FDE, and Capstone FDE.

faq.question: What will I be able to do after?
faq.answer: Stand up apps and RAG prototypes, run customer-style discovery, design solutions under constraints, scope POCs, deploy with monitoring, communicate with security and executives, and complete a capstone engagement.

faq.question: How should I split my time?
faq.answer: Weeks 1-6 focus on engineering and AI foundations (steps 1-2). Weeks 7-10 cover the FDE SDLC through enterprise AI (steps 3-9). Weeks 11-12 are the capstone project (step 10).

faq.question: What should I build to prove readiness?
faq.answer: Complete the capstone: discovery notes, ranked use cases, POC scope with pass mark, working prototype with evals, security Q&A, and an executive readout with handover documentation.

faq.question: Is progress saved? Do I need an account?
faq.answer: Progress is saved in your browser (localStorage). No login or backend is required for the FDE roadmap.

capstone.title: Capstone: An end-to-end customer engagement
capstone.intro: Run a realistic FDE engagement from discovery through handover: scoped POC, working prototype on representative data, security review prep, and executive readout.
deliverables: Discovery notes and a ranked use-case scorecard
A POC scope with a definition of done and an agreed pass mark
A working prototype on synthetic or public data, with evaluation results
Written answers to the ten questions a security team will ask
A 10-minute executive readout and a handover document

strongWork.title: Problem framing
strongWork.body: The chosen use case clearly follows from discovery and scoring, not from the technology you wanted to demo.

strongWork.title: Scope discipline
strongWork.body: The POC has a definition of done and a pass mark agreed before building starts.

strongWork.title: Technical delivery
strongWork.body: The prototype works on representative data, and evaluation results are honest about gaps.

strongWork.title: Trust and risk
strongWork.body: Security answers are specific, and risks have named owners and mitigations.

strongWork.title: Executive communication
strongWork.body: The readout leads with the decision and the evidence, without unnecessary jargon.
